<!--
Thanks for opening a PR. Fill in each section — if one truly doesn't apply, write "N/A" rather than deleting it, so reviewers know it wasn't skipped by accident.
-->

## Context
<!-- The business context worth knowing: what are we doing, and why does it matter right now? Assume the reviewer is smart but has zero context on this specific piece of work. -->

## Problem (or opportunity)
<!-- What's wrong, or what are we trying to achieve? -->

## Solution
<!-- How did you address it? Include:
- The approach you took
- Compromises you made (and why they were acceptable)
- Alternatives you considered and rejected (and why) -->

## Test
<!-- Why are you confident this is correct? How was it tested (unit/integration/manual/staging)?
Also note any scalability limit: how long should this hold before it needs revisiting (load, data volume, time, scope)? -->

## Demo
<!-- Screenshots, GIFs, or short clips when relevant. -->

## BTW
<!-- Drive-by fixes, cleanups, or anything else worth flagging that isn't central to the PR's main purpose. -->

---

**Why am I not just merging this myself?**
<!-- Every PR implicitly asks this. Be explicit about what you want from the reviewer:
- A sanity check before it ships?
- Domain expertise you don't have?
- A second pair of eyes on a risky/irreversible change?
- Sign-off required by process, not by judgment?
Naming this tells the reviewer what kind of attention to bring. -->
